items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: And you know what Bucky said? “Tell him to go home.” So I did. And that was our first date.

ctx.x: I was a registered nurse at St. Joseph’s Hospital in Paterson, New Jersey, and I had just graduated. It was in 1951, ’52, something like that. And I happened to look — I was on duty and I happened to look up, and sitting on the bench, they had a little bench outside the admitting department. And I had to go out and say, “may I help you.” So I walked out and this wonderful looking man, oh beautifully dressed, and I went out and I said, “may I help you.” And he said, “I’m waiting for my sister, Marie Pizzarelli.”…

you’re a celebrity and you worked with Vaughan Monroe, my favorite, my sister and I.” It was bliss. And so after that I was still living in the nursing school home and the phone rang while I was waiting for my brother to come pick me up to go home. And the phone rang, and it was Marie saying, and I happened to be there — I went to the phone, Marie said, “oh Ruth, my brother wants to talk to you” meaning Mr. Pizzarelli. He said, “hi Ruth, would you like to go out tonight?” I said, “oh I’d love to but I can’t go…
Gene Krupa. He had been arrested.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I went away for six weeks, with Ruth.

ctx.x: But then I went away with Benny Goodman in 1970, I went away for six weeks, with Ruth. I thought it was important to go with him because I always wanted to play with him. I had done a few gigs with him at the Waldorf, but this was a serious gig and I said let’s do it. So Ruth’s mother took care of the kids, sent them off to school. And all I had to do was leave in the morning and come back, and then six weeks later we were home and that was —
